author: l. c. boyd
title: UC Alumni Association to honor 18 alumni at annual celebration and unveil mural
text:
The University of Cincinnati Alumni Association announced on April 14 that it will host its annual Alumni Celebration during Alumni Week, which runs from April 13 to April 18. The event will feature a community art project and recognize 18 alumni for their achievements in various fields.
The celebration is scheduled for April 16 at the First Financial Center, also known as the Cincinnati Convention Center. This year’s honorees are being recognized for their innovation and impact on the university, their communities, and their professional fields.
Vinod Dham, who graduated from UC’s College of Engineering and Applied Science in 1977, will receive the William Howard Taft Medal for Notable Achievement. Dham is widely regarded as the “Father of the Pentium Chip” due to his pioneering work in semiconductor technology. He has more than four decades of experience in developing semiconductor products and venture capital. His accolades include being named among the top executives in the computer industry and one of America’s most influential Asian Americans. In addition, he was honored with India’s Padma Bhusan award in science and engineering in 2025.
Jennifer Heisey, UC’s chief alumni officer, said: “UC alumni demonstrate innovation and excellence in the widest range of disciplines while serving people around the world, and our 2026 honorees personify this institutional impact. Through their expertise, leadership and passion for their work, they make the world a better place. In the process, they reflect alumni success at the highest level, and we’re proud to recognize them this April during Alumni Week.”
As part of this year’s festivities, UCAA commissioned Chroma Projects to design a mural celebrating these achievements. The artwork is painted on a building at 1430 Vine Street in Cincinnati’s Over-the-Rhine neighborhood. It will be unveiled this month and remain on display through March next year.
Other awards include honors such as Robert E. Dobbs Distinguished Service Award given to Thomas D. Cassady; Marian A. Spencer Mosaic Award presented to Padma Chebrolu; Jeffrey Hurwitz Young Alumni Outstanding Achievement Award going to Ryan C. Marable; along with recognitions across UC’s colleges including Allied Health Sciences, Arts & Sciences, Business Administration (Blue Ash), Lindner College of Business (Clermont), Conservatory of Music (CCM), Design Architecture Art & Planning (DAAP), Education Criminal Justice & Human Services (CECH), Engineering & Applied Science (CEAS), Law School (Klekamp College), Medicine College Nursing Pharmacy Athletics.
The mural project highlights both individual achievement among UC graduates as well as collective contributions made by alumni over time.
